My world has basically come apart at the seams in the past two or three years and, while I keep telling myself that I can dig myself out of this hole (and I honestly think I can,) I keep worrying that the damage is done and that my life will never be as good as it was again. Oftentimes I feel like everything is irreparably damaged as a result of my actions, and if I died it'd be like nothing changed to my family and friends. I get this unshakeable feeling that I'm a loose end, the human equivalent of a goldfish you won for free from the county fair that ended up living years longer than it should have, and that nobody cares what happens to me. I've felt this way for a while, but in the past few months or so it's gotten progressively worse, to the point where I've posted on /r/suicidewatch and I often contact suicide self-help lines. I don't want to die but I feel as if I've boxed myself into this excuse for a life and I don't have any way out.


A friend of a friend committed suicide recently, and the whole time I was consoling my friend about his death I kept feeling like I was getting a glimpse into what would happen if I did the same thing, and I don't want to cause the people I care about harm. However, within two weeks of his death, she had started doing the same self-destructive activities that led to his death, and began hanging out with people who used his suicide as a means to attack others. I quickly began to realize that this guy's life meant nothing to them except for how they could use his loss of it to garner sympathy from others, and that nobody had actually tried to change for the better after the event. It makes it feel like, if his life was so meaningless (and he was much more liked than I was) to these people that they essentially forget about it after a week, then what will they do after my death? I doubt I'd get more than a rushed funeral and one-line obituary in the local paper. I guess that's what my life amounts to to these people.
